source_text:
Δευτέραν δὲ τάξει καὶ οὐδέν τι μικροτέραν ταύτης εἶναι
λέγει τό· »ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν·« οὐκοῦν τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ σεαυτόν. πυνθανομένου δὲ τοῦ προσδιαλεγομένου »τίς ἐστιν πλησίον;« οὐ τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον Ἰουδαίοις προωρίσατο τὸν πρὸς αἵματος οὐδὲ τὸν πολίτην οὐδὲ τὸν προσήλυτον οὐδὲ τὸν ὁμοίως περιτετμημένον οὐδὲ τὸν ἑνὶ καὶ ταὐτῷ νόμῳ χρώμενον· ἀλλὰ ἄνωθεν καταβαίνοντα ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἄγει τῷ λόγῳ τινὰ εἰς Ἱεριχὼ καὶ τοῦτον δείκνυσιν ὑπὸ λῃστῶν συγκεκεντημένον, ἐρριμμένον ἡμιθνῆτα ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, ὑπὸ ἱερέως παροδευόμενον, ὑπὸ Λευίτου παρορώμενον, ὑπὸ δὲ τοῦ Σαμαρείτου τοῦ ἐξωνειδισμένου καὶ ἀφωρισμένου κατελεούμενον, ὃς οὐχὶ κατὰ τύχην ὡς ἐκεῖνοι παρῆλθεν, ἀλλ᾿ ἧκε συνεσκευασμένος ὧν ὁ κινδυνεύων ἐδεῖτο, οἶνον, ἔλαιον, ἐπιδέσμους, κτῆνος, μισθὸν τῷ πανδοχεῖ, τὸν μὲν ἤδη διδόμενον, τὸν δὲ προσυπισχνούμενον. »τίς«, ἔφη, »τούτων γέγονε πλησίον τῷ τὰ δεινὰ παθόντι;« τοῦ δὲ ἀποκριναμένου ὅτι »ὁ τὸν ἔλεον πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπιδειξάμενος· καὶ σὺ τοίνυν πορευθεὶς οὕτω ποίει«, ὡς τῆς ἀγάπης βλαστανούσης εὐποιίαν.
thought_title: The neighbor is the one who shows mercy
orientation: Clement is explaining the second great commandment, love of neighbor, and how Jesus defined the neighbor through the parable of the Good Samaritan.
pass_a_gloss: And in second order and not at all smaller than this one, he says it is: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself"; therefore God above yourself. And when the one conversing with him asked, "Who is a neighbor?", he did not define for the Jews in the same manner the one related by blood, nor the citizen, nor the proselyte, nor the one circumcised in the same way, nor the one using one and the same law; but he leads by the word a certain man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he shows this man stabbed by robbers, thrown half-dead on the road, passed by by a priest, overlooked by a Levite, but pitied by the Samaritan, the one reviled and set apart, who did not pass by by chance as those others did, but came equipped with what the one in danger needed: wine, oil, bandages, a beast, pay for the innkeeper, the one already being given, the other being promised in addition. "Who," he said, "of these has become a neighbor to the one who suffered terrible things?" And when he answered that "the one who showed mercy toward him; and you then, go and do likewise," as love sprouting good-doing.

choices.why: Preserves the litotes and comparative force of the Greek, emphasizing the second commandment is not lesser than the first.

choices.english: the one reviled and set apart
choices.why: Renders the two participles literally, keeping the social exclusion of the Samaritan explicit.
Literal rendering of the compound adjective, preserving the vividness of the parable.
Keeps the participial metaphor of love as a plant producing good deeds, matching Clement's botanical image.
rejected: as love bears fruit in kindness

bible_refs.note: ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν

τίς ἐστιν πλησίον; ... ἄνωθεν καταβαίνοντα ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ... εἰς Ἱεριχὼ ... ὑπὸ λῃστῶν ... ἱερέως ... Λευίτου ... Σαμαρείτου ... οἶνον, ἔλαιον, ἐπιδέσμους, κτῆνος, μισθὸν τῷ πανδοχεῖ ... ὁ τὸν ἔλεον πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπιδειξάμενος ... πορευθεὶς οὕτω ποίει

pass_b_english: He says the second commandment is not at all smaller than this one: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” So then, love God more than yourself. When the man he was speaking with asked, “Who is my neighbor?” he did not define it the way the Jews did—not the blood relative, not the fellow citizen, not the convert, not the one circumcised in the same way, not the one who uses one and the same law. Instead, he leads the discussion to a man going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and shows him stabbed by robbers, thrown half-dead on the road, passed by a priest, overlooked by a Levite, but pitied by the Samaritan—the one reviled and set apart—who did not pass by as the others did by chance, but came equipped with what the man in danger needed: wine, oil, bandages, an animal, payment for the innkeeper—part given at once, part promised for later. “Which of these,” he said, “became a neighbor to the man who suffered these terrible things?” And when the man answered, “The one who showed mercy to him,” he said, “You go and do likewise,” since love sprouts good-doing.

fixed: Doubled word 'by by' in English; source has 'παροδευόμενον' (passed by), so removed the duplicate.

problems.source_quote: Δευτέραν δὲ τάξει καὶ οὐδέν τι μικροτέραν ταύτης εἶναι λέγει τό· »ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν·«
problems.why: Clement cites this as Jesus' words in the Gospel dialogue, not as Leviticus. The context is the lawyer's question and Jesus' reply (Luke 10:25-37), not a direct OT citation.
problems.fix: Remove '(Leviticus 19:18)' or replace with '(Luke 10:27)' or no citation.
problems.ruling: Greek lacks any citation; adding “(Leviticus 19:18)” misattributes source, altering Clement’s presentation.

edits.old: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18).
edits.new: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

fixed: Removed '(Leviticus 19:18)' because Clement presents this as Jesus' words in the Gospel dialogue (Luke 10:27), not as a direct Old Testament citation.

last_rejected.why: Wait—checking English: 'Which of these,' he said, 'became a neighbor to the man who suffered these terrible things?' This matches. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: English includes both τίς and γέγονε πλησίον as “Which of these … became a neighbor”.

last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ τὸν ἔλεον πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπιδειξάμενος
last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'mercy' for ἔλεος—'showed mercy' uses 'mercy', correct. No violation.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ τὸν ἔλεον … ἐπιδειξάμενος = “the one who showed mercy”, correctly rendered.
